entries.topicDescription: Navigating between screens and handling the back stack.

tips.title: A single Activity with multiple destinations simplifies shared state and transitions
tips.content:
Multiple Activities each maintain their own separate ViewModel scope and
task-stack entry, making it awkward to share state (a logged-in user
session, a shopping cart) across screens without passing everything
through Intent extras or a singleton.

The single-Activity pattern — one Activity hosting a NavHost with many
composable or fragment destinations — lets you scope a ViewModel to the
Activity itself and share it across destinations naturally, while shared-
element transitions and consistent navigation animations become simpler
to implement within one continuous navigation graph.

tips.title: NavHost and NavController basics
tips.content:
Jetpack Navigation uses a NavHost to display destinations
and a NavController to manage the back stack.

Define routes as strings (or type-safe objects in newer versions).
NavHost renders the composable for the current route.
NavController.navigate() pushes new destinations onto the stack.

Always hoist the NavController to the top-level composable
and pass callbacks down, not the controller itself.

tips.title: Pop back stack to avoid duplicates
tips.content:
By default, navigate() pushes a new instance onto the stack.
If the user taps a button twice, you get duplicate screens.

Use launchSingleTop to prevent duplicate destinations.
Use popUpTo to clear intermediate screens (e.g., going back to Home
after login should remove the login screen from the stack).

Think carefully about your back stack — users expect
the back button to behave predictably.

tips.title: Type-safe navigation with Kotlin serialization
tips.content:
String-based routes are error-prone — typos compile but crash at runtime.
Since Navigation 2.8, you can define routes as serializable data classes.

The compiler catches route mismatches at build time.
Arguments are type-safe — no more getString/getInt parsing.

This is the recommended approach for new Compose Navigation projects.
